releases.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 3.0.2
releases.source_notes:
**For the Innioasis Y1, Type A, on the Rondo 3.0 firmware.** An update you can install over Wi-Fi. With your own server, update it once to [Rondo server 3.1.0](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/releases/tag/server-v3.1.0) (its admin page offers it); from then on, Rondo and the server update apart.

- **Downloads are about three times faster.** A YouTube download now comes in four parts at once: a 10-minute 720p video took 50 seconds instead of 145, a two-hour episode about 8 minutes.
- **A download survives a dropout.** When the Wi-Fi or the internet goes away for a while, the download waits and carries on where it stopped, instead of failing or starting over (Software update's download too).
- **The Y1 stays awake while a download runs,** unplugged with the screen off too.
- **YouTube's pictures are back** in search, the feeds and on a download's row.
- **A download's row says what it's doing:** Downloading video, Downloading sound, Getting subtitles, Saving.
- **Rondo and the server have their own version numbers now.** Most releases change only the Y1, so they no longer ask you to update your server. This Rondo works with Rondo server 3.1.0 or newer; with an older one, Settings › YouTube › Connection, the dashboard and the YouTube screens say **Server needs an update**.

**How to get it**
- **On Rondo 3.0.x:** Settings › System › Software update, the dashboard's Overview, or the [update page](https://jarvissax.github.io/rondo/) over USB.
- **On Rondo 2.0 or earlier:** Innioasis Updater CE (Y1, Type A, Rondo 3.0.2), with **Keep my settings** turned on.

Files: `rondo-3.0.2.rondo` is the signed update bundle; `rom.zip` (the firmware) and `updater.png` are added by the release workflow a few minutes after publishing. Everything else: [changelog](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#302-november-12-2026).

releases.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 3.0.1
releases.source_notes:
**For the Innioasis Y1, Type A, on the Rondo 3.0 firmware.** An update you can install over Wi-Fi.

- **Charging shows on the battery.** On a charger or a computer, a green bolt shows next to the battery in the status bar and the YouTube headers, and the charge turns green.
- **YouTube and YouTube Music without internet.** With Wi-Fi off they now say "No Wi-Fi connection" at once instead of "Loading…", and load by themselves when Wi-Fi is back. On a Wi-Fi network without internet they give up after 30 seconds at most and say they couldn't reach YouTube.
- **Sharper subtitles.** Their lines sat between two rows of pixels, which blurred every letter.
- **The rest of SPWall is gone too:** its packet filter, code injector and renamed iptables, which nothing started, and the stock firmware's distribution tag. Rondo removes them itself when it updates, and the firmware leaves them out.

**How to get it**
- **On Rondo 3.0.0:** Settings › System › Software update, the dashboard's Overview, or the [update page](https://jarvissax.github.io/rondo/) over USB.
- **On Rondo 2.0 or earlier:** Innioasis Updater CE (Y1, Type A, Rondo 3.0.1), with **Keep my settings** turned on.

Files: `rondo-3.0.1.rondo` is the signed update bundle; `rom.zip` (the firmware) and `updater.png` are added by the release workflow a few minutes after publishing. Everything else: [changelog](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#301-november-12-2026).

releases.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 3.0.0
releases.source_notes:
**For the Innioasis Y1, Type A.** A new firmware without the stock firmware's root backdoors.

- **The root backdoors are gone.** Innioasis's own firmware, and so every Rondo firmware before this one, ran three programs as root that nothing on the Y1 needs:
  - `aggdll`, an app pusher's agent: a hidden `su` and a silent app installer;
  - `wifi_init`, a downloader it starts, which checks in with a server and runs what it downloads as root. That server doesn't answer today;
  - SPWall (`libsp.so`), which runs commands as root for other programs.

  This firmware leaves all three out, with what they left behind, and puts Android's own `am` back.
- **A Y1 installed again runs the firmware's own Rondo**, not an older update it took over Wi-Fi before.

**How to get it**
- **Innioasis Updater CE**: Y1, Type A, **Rondo**, 3.0.0. Turn on **Keep my settings** so your settings, Wi-Fi networks, server connection and paired headphones stay. Your music on the card is never touched.
- Software update on 2.0 shows 3.0.0 but can't install it, because the firmware itself has to change.

Files: `rondo-3.0.0.rondo` is the signed update bundle; `rom.zip` (the firmware) and `updater.png` are added by the release workflow a few minutes after publishing. Everything else: [changelog](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#300-november-12-2026).

releases.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 2.0.1
releases.source_notes:
**For the Innioasis Y1, Type A.** A fix release for Rondo 2.0.

- **Wi-Fi works after a fresh install.** On a Y1 that installed 2.0.0 without keeping its data, Wi-Fi never came on ("Wi-Fi didn't start"): Rondo powered the Wi-Fi chip on while its driver was still loading, and the chip stayed stuck until the next restart. Rondo now waits for the driver first (#3).
- **Next and Previous in Now Playing slide smoothly:** the slide starts on the press, and the covers of the songs before and after are ready before you press.

**How to get it**
- **Wi-Fi not working on 2.0.0?** Install with **Innioasis Updater CE** (Y1, Type A, Rondo 2.0.1), or over USB from the [update page](https://jarvissax.github.io/rondo/) in Chrome or Edge.
- **Wi-Fi working:** Settings › System › Software update, or the dashboard's Overview.
- **Coming from 1.0:** Innioasis Updater CE, with **Keep Data** to keep your settings.

Files: `rondo-2.0.1.rondo` is the signed update bundle; `rom.zip` (the firmware) and `updater.png` are added by the release workflow a few minutes after publishing. Everything else: [changelog](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#201-november-12-2026).

releases.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 2.0.0
releases.source_notes:
**For the Innioasis Y1, Type A.** A new firmware: install `rom.zip` with **Innioasis Updater CE** (choose **Keep Data** to keep your settings when coming from 1.0). After that, Rondo updates itself over Wi-Fi from GitHub.

Rondo 2.0 is rebuilt as a program of its own: Android's app layer is gone, the Y1 starts straight into Rondo, and everything runs smoother at 60 frames a second.

- **YouTube and YouTube Music straight from the Y1**, no server needed (your own server is optional and still works). Sign in with a code, like a smart TV.
- **Subtitles** on YouTube videos and on the videos on the card, in a look of your own (YouTube's by default).
- **Download YouTube videos** at 720p, 480p or 360p, with their subtitles, to watch offline.
- **Library in four:** Music (with Cover Flow, album artists, genres, smart playlists), Videos, Photos and Files.
- **Sound:** an equalizer for each output, Headphone match (with a server), loudness boost, volume leveling, the amplifier and a volume limit.
- **Software update from GitHub**, with or without a server; the dashboard has every setting too.

Everything else is in the [changelog](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#200-november-11-2026).

Files: `rondo-2.0.0.rondo` is the signed update bundle; `rom.zip` (the firmware) and `updater.png` are added by the release workflow a few minutes after publishing.

releases.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 1.0.2
releases.source_notes:
Rondo 1.0.2 is about the server: it now updates itself with one click from its admin page. **Nothing changes on the Y1 itself**; it still offers this version as an update so the Y1 and the server stay on the same number.

## What's new

- **Update the server with one click.** When a newer Rondo is out, the server's admin page offers **Update**: the server downloads the new version and restarts on it in a minute or two, keeping your settings, YouTube account and connected Y1. A small companion container, `rondo-updater`, does the work; it only ever touches the Rondo server's own container, and if the new version doesn't start, the old one comes back by itself.
- **Ready-made server images.** Installing the server now downloads it instead of building it on your machine, for regular PCs and 64-bit ARM (Raspberry Pi 4 and 5, many NAS boxes). The first start is much quicker on small machines.

The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Moving your server over

A server set up before 1.0.2 built itself and has no updater yet. Update it by hand once, and **Update** on the admin page does it from then on:

```bash
cd rondo
git pull
docker compose -f infra/compose.home.yaml pull      # or compose.vps.yaml
docker compose -f infra/compose.home.yaml up -d
```

Your admin password, YouTube account and connected Y1 stay. Details: [Keeping it running](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/docs/server.md#keeping-it-running).

## The Y1

If your Y1 runs Rondo 1.0.1, **Settings › Software update**, **Install** in the dashboard or [the update page](https://jarvissax.github.io/rondo/) bring it to 1.0.2 in a minute; nothing else changes. New to Rondo: choose **Rondo** in [Innioasis Updater CE](https://innioasis.app) (Y1, then Type A), or install `rom.zip` below with the Updater's **Settings › Install from a file…**. Only for the **Y1 Type A**.

## Files

- `rom.zip`: the firmware, for Innioasis Updater CE (Y1 Type A), built from `rondo-1.0.2.apk` by the release workflow.
- `rondo-1.0.2.apk`: the update, for a Y1 that already runs the Rondo firmware.
- `updater.png`: the picture Innioasis Updater CE shows for this release.
- The server images: `ghcr.io/jarvissax/rondo-server:1.0.2` and `ghcr.io/jarvissax/rondo-updater:1.0.2` (also `latest`).

releases.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 1.0.1
releases.source_notes:
A small update to Rondo for the **Innioasis Y1, Type A**. If your Y1 already runs Rondo, it installs over the one you have in about a minute, and everything stays: settings, Wi-Fi, server connection, playlists and music.

## What's new

- **Click sound stays off.** Turning off **Settings › Click sound** (or the switch in the dashboard) now lasts through a restart. Before, the Y1's own sound profile turned the click back on every time it started.
- **Every release now comes with its firmware.** The `rom.zip` that Innioasis Updater CE installs is built automatically for each release, so a new install always gets the newest Rondo.
- **Rondo knows which updates it can install.** The firmware now carries a version of its own. If a future release changes the firmware itself, not only Rondo, Settings › Software update, the dashboard and the update page say so and point you to Innioasis Updater CE, instead of offering an install that couldn't work.
- **One place for news of a release.** The Y1 (through your server), the dashboard and the update page all learn about a new Rondo from the update page, once its firmware is ready, so they always agree with each other and with Innioasis Updater CE.
- **New README and guides**, with screenshots.

The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Updating from 1.0.0

Pick whichever is handiest; none of them reinstalls the firmware:

- **On the Y1:** Settings › Software update, then **Install now** (needs your Rondo server).
- **In the dashboard:** Settings › Dashboard on the Y1, open it on your phone, press **Install**.
- **Over USB:** open [the update page](https://jarvissax.github.io/rondo/) in Chrome or Edge and plug the Y1 in.

If you run a Rondo server, update it too ([how](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/docs/server.md#keeping-it-running)); it's 1.0.1 as well.

## Installing for the first time

Choose **Rondo** in [Innioasis Updater CE](https://innioasis.app) (Y1, then Type A), or download `rom.zip` below and use the Updater's **Settings › Install from a file…**. Installing replaces everything on the Y1 itself; **the microSD card isn't touched**. The [install guide](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/docs/install.md) has the details.

Only for the **Y1 Type A** (players that shipped with software 2.0.0 or later), not the Type B or the Y2.

## Files

- `rom.zip`: the firmware, for Innioasis Updater CE (Y1 Type A). Built from `rondo-1.0.1.apk` by this repository's release workflow, a few minutes after publishing.
- `rondo-1.0.1.apk`: the update, for a Y1 that already runs the Rondo firmware.
- `updater.png`: the picture Innioasis Updater CE shows for this release.

releases.title: Portable Flashing Package: Rondo 1.0.0
releases.source_notes:
Rondo is now a firmware for the Innioasis Y1: the Y1 starts straight into Rondo's click-wheel menus, with nothing else on it.

**For the Y1, Type A only** (players that shipped with software 2.0.0 or later). Not for the Type B or the Y2.

## Install

Choose **Rondo** in [Innioasis Updater CE](https://innioasis.app) (Y1, Type A). Or download `rom.zip` below and use the Updater's **Settings › Install from a file…**.

Installing replaces everything on the Y1 itself: the original player, Rockbox, settings. **The microSD card isn't touched**, so your music stays. When the Updater is done, press the Y1's Power button; the first start takes a couple of minutes. The [install guide](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/docs/install.md) has the details and the first steps after it.

For YouTube Music and YouTube, [set up a Rondo server](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/docs/server.md) with Docker, at home or on a VPS.

## Updates

Later versions install over this one in a minute, without flashing again, keeping your settings, Wi-Fi, playlists and music: **Settings › Software update** on the Y1, **Install** in the dashboard, or [the update page](https://jarvissax.github.io/rondo/) over USB.

## What's in it

- iPod-style menus for the click wheel, with optional vibration and a click on every step
- Your music and videos from the microSD card, with covers, lyrics, search and playlists
- The card as a USB drive when the Y1 is plugged into a computer
- YouTube Music and YouTube, streamed live through your own server, including Shorts, with or without a YouTube account
- FM radio with station names, scanning and saved stations
- Bluetooth headphones and speakers, and Wi-Fi, set up from the wheel
- A dashboard in your phone's browser for music, playlists, settings, the theme, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, the radio and updates
- Shut down and restart from Settings, or by holding the Power button

## Good to know

- Only the Y1 Type A is supported; the Type B and Y2 haven't been tested.
- Rockbox, the original player and Android's own Settings aren't part of Rondo. Innioasis Updater CE puts any of them back.
- YouTube Music and YouTube need your own Rondo server; the card, the radio and Bluetooth don't.

## Files

| File | What it is | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rom.zip` | The firmware, for Innioasis Updater CE (Y1 Type A) | `97855240680f2f71f0e33147bd6f7567f4bf17e2efb082d495dc55b2877a0b6c` |
| `rondo-1.0.0.apk` | Rondo by itself: updates a Y1 that runs the Rondo firmware | `911edd65b8f375e452c05e2004c1c817215a65f9a56d023c5acfb9a7d0857edd` |
| `updater.png` | The picture Innioasis Updater CE shows for this release | `40b9f5679e2f84b4dd7c6fda968abf702df3ccb6b743fcb88e142eeb8b52047e` |

The firmware is built with [`firmware/build.sh`](https://github.com/jarvissax/rondo/blob/main/firmware/build.sh) from the y1-community's [Android 4.2 base ROM](https://github.com/y1-community/y1-ata-rom) (0.1, Type A). Its scatter file, preloader and flashing files are the base ROM's, unchanged.
